While kerbals spend a lot of time reaching out \ninto space, getting around on Kerbin is another \nof their pastimes.
You'll hopefully learn some tricks in this section \nto go from this pile of parts to the below levels \nof awesome!
Designing a plane that will fly is all about balancing the four aero \nforces. In construction you can use the UI helpers to apply some\ncommon ideas to help you succeed.
Of course, once you have a firm grasp of flight, imagination (and physics) are the only limits.
Here are some basic themes that help build simple planes.
The center of lift should be near the center of mass.
Build your plane around a "center line."
Line up the CoT to push through the CoM.
Here are some examples of planes that suffer from balance issues. \nHopefully you can learn a thing or two from our mistakes.
The thrust in this design is pushing the plane around \nthe CoM, not through it. This is a CoT Issue.
Here the center of lift is off the center-line.\nThis plane will roll left quite badly.
Lastly the CoL here is well behind the \nCoM, this plane will pitch down hard.
The CoL is found by adding the individual lift components from all \nparts of the craft. Lift is generated by wings, control surfaces and \neven some fuselage parts (via an effect called body lift).
When designing an aircraft one of the key indicators is the center \nof lift (CoL). Its location is crucial to the balance of the plane.
Note: In game you will only see the CoL marker in the construction interface.
Control surface lift not shown,\nbut you should get the idea.
When building a vessel you will use a number of control parts, and there are two types of parts to \nconsider. Having one type and not the other will leave you floundering for control.
These parts apply force to the vessel - via airflow over \nsurfaces, torque from gyroscopes, gimballed engine\nmovement and direct thrust from thrusters.
These parts allow you to input controls \nto the vessel.
Note: You create flaps using ailerons and disabling the three control axis. You then \n deploy them using part actions or action groups.
